paths.description: Homepage and today listing: primary discovery task, consent, responsive layout, performance, privacy and accessibility.
Rai 1 channel detail: representative channel schedule/detail template and route continuity.
First-run prime-time page: representative filtered/listing archetype.
Tomorrow page: representative date-navigation journey and repeated listing template.

findings.guidanceCategory: user-experience
findings.summary: The fixed black palette does not follow the user’s light/dark preference.
findings.evidence: The light/default and prefers-color-scheme: dark captures retain the same black page; the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and no prefers-color-scheme, color-scheme, or light-dark() CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map surfaces/text through preference-aware tokens, while preserving the existing dark presentation for users who prefer it.

findings.guidanceCategory: Programme cards and controls include text below WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.summary: Lighthouse accessibility found white text on Rai 3 green at 3.77:1, white text on Italia 1 blue at 4.47:1, and the Pagina 2 button at 3.65:1. The stylesheet also has no forced-colors or prefers-contrast adaptation.
findings.evidence: Darken affected channel colors or use an accessible foreground token, test every channel palette, and add forced-colors/high-contrast styles that retain control boundaries.

findings.guidanceCategory: Navigation between the long listing and channel/detail pages swaps abruptly.
findings.summary: Static MPA links were exercised between four templates; the probe finds no authored view-transition CSS and no cross-document @view-transition rule.
findings.evidence: Progressively enhance same-origin page changes with cross-document View Transitions and a no-motion fallback.

findings.guidanceCategory: The 7,445 px homepage provides no persistent position or progress cue.
findings.summary: The mobile full-page capture shows a very long sequence of channel cards; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, sticky shrinking header, or progress indicator, and navigation controls disappear far above the current card.
findings.evidence: Keep a compact channel/date navigator available while scrolling and expose position/progress without obscuring content.

findings.guidanceCategory: A consent wall obscures the primary TV listings on every fresh page load.
findings.summary: Desktop, mobile, and channel screenshots show a modal covering the first viewport before interaction, with the page dimmed behind it.
findings.evidence: Minimise pre-consent collection and present a compact, accessible consent choice with equally direct accept/reject actions; avoid blocking the schedule where consent is not required.

findings.guidanceCategory: Large empty ad slots and dense icon chrome push schedules far below the fold.
findings.summary: The full-page mobile capture contains large blank regions between programme groups and repeated icon grids at both ends; useful schedule content occupies a minority of several viewport-height segments.
findings.evidence: Collapse unfilled ad slots, reserve only bounded ad space, and simplify repeated icon/navigation chrome around the schedule.

findings.guidanceCategory: Components only adapt through viewport media queries, not their available container.
findings.summary: The site stylesheet has three @media blocks but zero @container rules; reused channel cards are laid out by global viewport assumptions.
findings.evidence: Add container-type to reusable listing regions and use size-aware container queries for card composition, with current media rules as fallback.

findings.guidanceCategory: Many primary links and buttons are too small and keyboard focus is not visibly styled.
findings.summary: The probe measured [continua] links at 56×15 px and programme buttons at 223×21 px; focusing the first navigation link produced outline-style none.
findings.evidence: Give controls at least a 24×24 CSS px target (prefer 44×44 for touch), add spacing around inline links, and define a high-contrast :focus-visible ring.

findings.guidanceCategory: Missing site resources and routes fall back to a bare Apache 404 with no recovery.
findings.summary: Both /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml returned the default Apache 404 document, which provides no site navigation, search, or route back to the schedule.
findings.evidence: Serve an intentional branded 404/error page with a route back to today’s schedule; distinguish retryable network failures from missing pages.

findings.guidanceCategory: Cold-load performance and visual stability miss the Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.summary: Lighthouse measured LCP 13.9 s and CLS 0.222; raw-CDP mobile layout measured CLS 0.109 on home and 0.243 on the Rai 1 detail. The trace was fast in a separate warm-like run (LCP 1.15 s), so the slow-path variance itself needs attention.
findings.evidence: Reserve all late content, prioritise the actual LCP element, and delay consent/ad work that competes with primary schedule rendering.

findings.guidanceCategory: Third-party JavaScript dominates transfer and much of it is unused on load.
findings.summary: HAR recorded 580,101 script bytes out of 774,849 total transferred bytes; Lighthouse estimated 266 KiB of unused JavaScript and 14 KiB of unused CSS.
findings.evidence: Load analytics/advertising only after the relevant consent and need, remove duplicate integrations, and conditionally load below-fold media.

findings.guidanceCategory: Programme artwork and embedded videos lack accessible alternatives.
findings.summary: The image primitive found 8 of 11 images without alt text; the DOM probe found untitled YouTube iframes, and Lighthouse failed the frame-title audit.
findings.evidence: Add concise programme-title alt text where artwork is meaningful, empty alt for decoration, and descriptive title attributes for every embedded video.

findings.guidanceCategory: The document lacks useful landmarks and the consent UI overwhelms the heading outline.
findings.summary: The probe found no header/nav/main/aside/footer landmarks. On home, consent markup introduced multiple H1s plus hundreds of vendor H2s, while focused navigation had outline-style none.
findings.evidence: Add semantic landmarks and one page H1, keep consent headings within a coherent dialog structure, and make focus order/rings match reading order.

findings.guidanceCategory: Schedule text is dense and frequently rendered at small sizes.
findings.summary: The mobile screenshot shows long 14 px schedule lines and 15 px-high continuation links packed into saturated cards, with little line spacing or grouping.
findings.evidence: Increase body/interactive text size and line-height, group times and titles semantically, and use text wrapping and spacing tokens for scanability.

findings.guidanceCategory: The page logs mixed-content errors and triggers browser hygiene failures.
findings.summary: Lighthouse captured repeated blocked requests for http://www.staseraintv.com/favicon.ico, reported an inspector issue, and found a BFCache failure.
findings.evidence: Change every same-site asset URL to HTTPS or relative URLs, then resolve the reported inspector and BFCache blockers.

findings.guidanceCategory: Every audited image lacks explicit dimensions and responsive delivery.
findings.summary: The image primitive found 11/11 images without width/height, 9/11 without srcset, 8 below-fold images without lazy loading, and all 11 in legacy PNG/JPEG formats.
findings.evidence: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, use responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold artwork, and encode suitable assets as WebP/AVIF.

findings.guidanceCategory: Canonical discovery infrastructure is incomplete.
findings.summary: The probe found no canonical URL, while /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml both returned HTTP 404. Public pages otherwise returned 200 and explicitly allowed indexing.
findings.evidence: Publish robots.txt and an XML sitemap, add self-referencing canonicals, and keep those signals consistent across today/tomorrow/channel templates.

findings.guidanceCategory: TV listings have no structured or social-preview metadata.
findings.summary: Across home and Rai 1 templates the probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph tags despite visible programme/channel entities.
findings.evidence: Add accurate schema.org BroadcastEvent/TVSeries or ItemList data where appropriate, plus Open Graph title, description, image, and canonical URL.

findings.guidanceCategory: Transport is HTTPS, but browser-enforced security headers and cookie protections are absent.
findings.summary: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. All five observed cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None; Lighthouse also found an HTTP favicon request.
findings.evidence: Set HSTS, a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; use HTTPS-only Secure cookies and the least-permissive SameSite value.

findings.guidanceCategory: Tracking and consent scope are disproportionate to a simple TV schedule.
findings.summary: Before any visible consent choice was made, the tracker primitive saw 8 third-party origins and four known tracker hosts; the consent dialog states that 210 partners may process device/personal data, while long-lived analytics/consent cookies last 390–400 days.
findings.evidence: Default to no optional tracking, reduce vendors and retention, gate all analytics/ads until consent, and provide a one-click reject choice equal to accept.

findings.guidanceCategory: Date/time output is hard-coded for one locale and layout CSS relies on physical directions.
findings.summary: The probe found Italian lang but rendered fixed numeric dates such as 19/07/2026; stylesheet inspection found 29 left/right physical-property uses and no evidence of locale-aware formatting or logical properties.
findings.evidence: Format dates/times with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the declared locale and replace layout-critical left/right properties with inline/block logical equivalents.

findings.guidanceCategory: Third-party scripts, fonts, trackers, and eager media outweigh the site’s simple content task.
findings.summary: HAR transferred 775 KB across 40 requests, including 580 KB of script; 8 third-party origins loaded and 8 below-fold images were eager, despite the core experience being text schedules and small artwork.
findings.evidence: Set a route-level byte budget, defer below-fold embeds/images, self-host or trim fonts, and remove or consent-gate low-value third parties.

taskList.title: Remove the blocking, over-broad pre-consent tracking experience
Fix LCP/CLS and reserve all media/ad space
Restore semantic structure, alternatives, focus, targets, and contrast
Deploy transport headers and secure cookie policy
Trim and defer third-party code and media
Publish canonical, robots, sitemap, and entity metadata
Add preference-aware theming and high-contrast support
Simplify chrome and add long-page navigation cues
Add intentional error recovery and resilient 404 handling
Modernise container responsiveness, transitions, and locale formatting
